notes: Original 2016 release (as described in this paper): 50 subjects performing 9 ADLs + 54 subjects simulating 4 fall types. Sensors: accelerometer, gyroscope, orientation of a Samsung Galaxy S3 (LSM330DLC inertial module). Sampling rate ~100 Hz (Android SENSOR_DELAY_FASTEST); phone placed loosely in a trouser pocket at a random orientation. Paper uses 1.28 s windows with 50% overlap for HAR benchmarking. NOTE: the current public 'Second Release' on the BMI/HMU site is an EXTENDED version with 66 subjects, 12 ADLs + 4 falls + 1 daily-living scenario, >3200 trials (often cited as MobiAct v2.0 / Chatzaki et al. 2017, Springer CCIS DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-62704-5_7). Verify which release the HALO code actually uses. Data distributed by the Biomedical Informatics & eHealth Lab, Hellenic Mediterranean University (formerly TEI of Crete).
